answer: In an agent market for dune surveys, each seller must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before posting offers in a job thread. The contract requires a separate bond for every identity, so creating 1,000 sellers ties up $100,000 for a month. Through the prism of this rule, a new name carries a measurable capital cost. An attacker can still buy influence, but cannot multiply eligible identities merely by generating free keys.
